topic: Representation: equal-amount equation where solving cannot pick the model
problem: Tank A contains 500 liters of water and is being drained at a constant rate of 12 liters per minute. At the same time, tank B, which contains 80 liters of water, is being filled at a constant rate of 20 liters per minute. Which equation can be used to find t, the number of minutes after which the two tanks contain the same amount of water?

bad.why: Graphing and finding t = 13.125 answers a question that was not asked, and it cannot pick the model: 500 - 20t = 80 + 12t has the same solution, so two choices would look correct.
Solving every choice and comparing solutions is calculator work on the wrong task; the first two choices share the solution t = 13.125.
Building and solving the story's equations goes past the task, which ends once the model matches a choice.

algebraFirst.description: Writes 500 - 12t = 80 + 20t, then solves it (t = 13.125) and checks which choices give that value, which cannot separate the first two choices.

explanationNotes: The task is only to write the model, not solve it. Tank A starts at 500 and loses 12 each minute (500 - 12t), tank B starts at 80 and gains 20 each minute (80 + 20t), and 'contain the same amount' sets these equal. Warn that solving is a trap here: 500 - 20t = 80 + 12t swaps the two rates yet has the same solution, so checking solutions cannot tell which model is right.
